implementerProof.how: This round retires the model that the evictor's ceiling carries the listener's ping — the thing my round-11 measurement showed to be false — from the places that still taught it. So the verification is of the prose against the code it cites, plus the rows whose failure text now states the corrected claim. Both claims check: staleRoomRetryBackoffMax is 2 * pglisten.DefaultListenIdle, which is the minute the comment now promises, and listenerPoolSize is 1 with exactly three permanent callers of Pool.Listener in the tree — the delivery hub (api/delivery_live_hub.go:328), the event stream relay (api/event_stream_relay.go:123) and the stale-room evictor (docs/stale_room.go:122) — which is what the rewritten pool comment names.
implementerProof.whatTheProofDidNotCover: Unchanged from rounds 9 to 11 and not widened: the evictor's arming, backoff and in-flight branch are each pinned at their own seam in the docs package with a control I drove, and none is reachable from outside the process. Nothing this round adds to that boundary or takes from it.

proof.criterion: The prose this round rewrites is true of the code it cites — the claim that failed review twice before, in the opposite direction, when a comment asserted an invariant the code did not hold.
proof.surface: The repository's own source at this head, each claim read against the construct it names.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && grep -n 'staleRoomRetryBackoffMax\s*=' internal/dispatch/docs/stale_room.go; grep -n 'listenerPoolSize\s*=' internal/dispatch/store/pool.go; grep -rn 'Pool.Listener' --include=*.go internal/dispatch | grep -v _test
proof.observed: staleRoomRetryBackoffMax = 2 * pglisten.DefaultListenIdle (stale_room.go:476), so the comment's 'one wake a minute instead of one every staleRoomEvictInterval' is the ceiling the code has. listenerPoolSize = 1 (pool.go:234), and Pool.Listener has exactly the three permanent callers the rewritten comment names, no more. The ceiling's comment now says it carries nothing for the ping and points at the listener's own stamp and cap, which is what round 11 measured and what the ping now rests on.
proof.negativeControl: The control for a comment is the claim it would have to contradict, and this round's rewrite exists because round 11's measurement contradicted the old one: the ceiling does not keep the ping alive, since waitFor's cap and listen's stamp are one mechanism of the listener's own (491.9/487.2/482.6 ms with the guard, 493.2/484.9/482.7 ms with the separable part reverted — indistinguishable). A reader who takes the new comment at its word and goes looking will find the constants above rather than a promise nothing holds.

proof.criterion: The rows whose failure text this round rewrote still fail for the reason their new text states.
proof.surface: The docs package against the real Postgres, and a scratch clone with the backoff flattened.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && . /legion/harness/env.sh && go test -count=3 -timeout 1800s -run 'Evict|ReExamin|BacksOff|BurstEvicts|ListenerWasDown' ./internal/dispatch/docs/ && go test -count=3 -timeout 1800s ./internal/dispatch/pglisten/
proof.observed: ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs 43.825s and ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/pglisten 44.062s, three consecutive runs each. On a scratch clone of this head with staleRoomRetryBackoff flattened to one interval, the row fails with its new text: `after 8 re-examinations that reached no verdict the room is still re-armed 2s out, under the listener's 30s idle period and so under the ceiling of twice it: the backoff is not climbing to its bound, so a room nothing writes to again goes on re-reading its head through the pool - and, while it is still behind, under the document's lock - at that rate for the life of the process`. The message now says what the backoff is for — a rate bound on one room's reads — rather than that it keeps the ping alive, and the row still catches its removal.
proof.negativeControl: The flattened-backoff clone is the control, and it is the same one I drove in round 10 against the old text: the row's verdict is unchanged and only its account of itself has moved. A rewritten failure message that no longer matched what makes the row fail would be the defect this check exists for.

notes: What I did not re-run, and why, stated rather than left to be noticed: the two-process package and the browser suite. The commit changes no compiled behaviour — comments and two t.Fatalf strings, shown by the diff command in `scope` — and both were green at round 11's head, which is this head's parent in every respect that compiles. CI's dispatch-multiprocess and dispatch jobs are green here besides. If a reviewer wants either re-taken on this exact head, say so and I will, but I would rather name the omission than spend an hour proving a comment.

The correction of round 11 stands in the pull request body as well as here: the stamp and the cap are one mechanism in the code, not two, so the limit on that row is a property of the design and not a gap a better row could close. This round's comments are consistent with that, which is the point of the round.

The stopping rule (comment 9ab8bf0a) did not fire this round either: no new finding in the mechanism, so the evictor-side backoff stays. If a later round fires it, removing the backoff must take TestARoomThatKeepsGettingNoAnswerBacksOffPastTheListenersIdlePeriod with it — that row passes only because the backoff is there, and its new failure text names the backoff's purpose explicitly, which makes the pairing easier to see and no less necessary.
Round 5's three bounds on the period gate, round 8's severity table and rounds 9 to 11's proof boundary are unchanged at this head.
